Description: Cross-polarized backscatter sensitive to volumetric scattering from branches and stems, widely used for biomass estimation.
Co-polarized backscatter primarily interacting with trunks and ground, reflecting surface roughness and soil moisture.
Angular Second Moment (ASM) measures the uniformity of the image; high values indicate a homogeneous canopy structure.
Sum Average provides a mean intensity measure within the texture window, smoothing out speckle noise to reveal trends.
Cluster Shade assesses the skewness of the gray-level matrix, sensitive to shadowing effects caused by canopy height variations.
Correlation measures the linear dependency of gray levels, capturing the spatial arrangement and periodicity of forest structure.
Indicates vegetation greenness and photosynthetic capacity; broadly used but can saturate in high biomass regions.
Improves upon NDVI by decoupling the canopy background signal and reducing atmospheric influences.
Minimizes the effect of bare soil background, providing better accuracy in open or sparse forest areas.
Monitors vegetation water content and stress levels using NIR and SWIR bands, critical for forest health.
Sensitive to liquid water in vegetation canopies, effectively distinguishing water stress from other variations.
specific for assessing equivalent water thickness in leaves and soil background moisture.
Blue band (Visible), useful for atmospheric correction and separating vegetation from soil lines.
Green band (Visible), captures the peak reflection of healthy vegetation due to chlorophyll content.
Red band (Visible), the primary absorption band for chlorophyll, essential for calculating vegetation indices.
Short-wave Infrared 1 (SWIR1), highly sensitive to moisture content in vegetation and soil.
Short-wave Infrared 2 (SWIR2), aids in discriminating dry plant matter and geological features.
